validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real and operating. This is Malaysia's flagship gas transmission trunk system, independently documented by PETRONAS Gas Berhad's own current operator page, English Wikipedia, and a contemporaneous 1996-era Oil & Gas Journal article on Stage III construction — three genuinely independent origins (not one wire story reprinted, none citing GEM). Both gem.wiki-cited leads that were checked failed live: the 2018 petronas.com.my URL now 502s and the petronas.com/mpm/malaysia-e-p/overview URL 404s; the two still-live wiki citations (PGB gas-transportation page, en.wikipedia.org Peninsula Gas Utilisation) were re-verified live and are the basis for this finding, not the dead ones. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk (Fuel=Gas), not a gathering/feeder line — confirmed by all three sources describing a 2,623 km, 3,500 MMcf/d cross-peninsula transmission mainline. DUPLICATE: checked against the other 4 in-scope rows — no overlap. P7105 (Malaysia–Singapore) is the short cross-border segment beyond PGU's own Johor/Singapore export lateral (route-adjacent, not the same pipe); P1068 (TTM) lands at Songkhla, Thailand, a different corridor from PGU's own Perlis terminus; P1066/P1067 are East Malaysia (Sabah/Sarawak) systems entirely. No relabel/segment-double-count risk. SPEC — Length: 2,623 km confirmed at high tier (PETRONAS PGB page states '2,623 km' directly; Wikipedia independently states '2,623 km (1,630 mi)'; both agree exactly). SPEC — Capacity: 3,500 MMcf/d (sheet: CapacityUnits=MMcf/d) confirmed at high tier (PETRONAS PGB page: 'capacity to transport up to 3,500 mmscfd'; mmscfd and MMcf/d are the same unit, no conversion needed). SPEC — Endpoints: StartLocation Kertih confirmed by all three sources as the original Stage I terminus/GPP site. EndLocation Kangar (Perlis) is directionally correct — Wikipedia's Phase III description ends at 'Arau, Perlis' and OGJ's Stage III description ends at 'Pauh in Perlis'; Kangar, Arau, and Pauh are all within a few km of each other in the same Perlis district near the Malaysia-Thailand border, so this reads as a minor location-precision variance across sources rather than a wrong endpoint — flagged as a caveat only. FuelSource='Terengganu Gas Field' is correct for the pipeline's origin (GPP1 Kertih processes offshore Terengganu-basin gas, per Wikipedia's Phase I account) but is now incomplete as a description of current supply: PETRONAS's own page states the system has grown to four entry points (Kertih, Pengerang, Sungai Udang, and an entry from Thailand), so gas now also arrives via LNG regasification (Pengerang, Sungai Udang) and the TTM interconnection, not solely the original Terengganu field. Not a wrong value, but an incomplete one — flagged as a caveat, not a hard concern.

validity.recommendation: Verify/correct StartYear1=1993 — no independent source names 1993 as a PGU milestone. Consider either correcting StartYear1 to 1984 (Phase I, first gas at Kertih) and using StartYear2/StartYear3 to record the 1992 Singapore-export extension and the ~1996-1998 Perlis extension (which is what actually brings the route to the full Kertih->Perlis/Kangar extent and 2,623 km length recorded on this row), or documenting in ResearcherNotes which specific 1993 milestone the sheet intends.
validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1=1993 does not match any documented PGU milestone in the two independent sources that give a construction timeline. Wikipedia (independent secondary source): Phase I completed 1984 (Kertih GPP + 32 km pipeline), Phase II completed 1992 (extension west/south to Singapore), Phase III completed 1998 (Meru→Perlis extension, i.e. the segment that reaches this row's own EndLocation). Oil & Gas Journal (independent trade press, contemporaneous ~1996 reporting on Stage III): Stage III Sector 1 (Meru→Lumut, 184 km + Segari lateral) completed Q1 1996; Sectors 2&3 (Lumut→Pauh, 264 km + Prai/Teknologi Tenaga Perlis laterals) followed. Neither source places any phase completion in 1993 — the closest documented dates bracketing it are 1992 (Phase II) and 1996-1998 (Phase III/Stage III). Since this row's own recorded length (2,623 km) and endpoints (Kertih→Perlis) only exist once Phase III/Stage III is complete, a single StartYear1=1993 understates when the full route described on this row was actually finished, and doesn't correspond to any single phase's completion either. This is a genuine, if modest, spec mismatch worth a research follow-up rather than a silent pass.

validity.recommendation: Correct Owner1 from 'Petronas' 100% to 'Petronas Gas Berhad' (PGB) — the entity PETRONAS's own site names as the actual owner/operator of the PGU pipeline system — and verify PGB's exact current shareholding structure before assigning any parent-level percentage; PGB is a separately incorporated, Bursa Malaysia-listed company that has NOT been wholly owned by parent PETRONAS since its 1995 IPO, so 100% is very unlikely to be correct for either the parent or PGB depending on which entity the field is meant to record.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet records Owner1='Petronas' at 100%. PETRONAS's own official gas-transportation page states the PGU system 'is owned and operated by Petronas Gas Berhad' — a distinct, separately incorporated subsidiary (PGB, Bursa Malaysia ticker PETGAS), not the ultimate parent group 'Petronas' (Petroliam Nasional Berhad) directly. Independently, English Wikipedia's Petronas article confirms PGB has been a publicly listed company since its 1995 IPO on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, i.e. NOT a wholly-owned subsidiary of the parent — general market/investor-relations reporting found during this check consistently describes PETRONAS's stake in PGB as roughly half (~51%), with the remainder publicly traded, though I could not pin an exact current percentage to a single fully-verifiable citable page (a PGB Bursa filing PDF returned an ambiguous/likely-boilerplate '100%' holding-company statement that conflicts with PGB's known public-listing status, so I am not citing that figure). Two independent sources agree the asset-owning/operating entity is PGB, not the parent, and that PGB is not wholly parent-owned — that much is a solid attribution finding; the exact percentage split needs a follow-up look at a current PGB annual report/Bursa shareholding disclosure before writing a number to the sheet.

summary: P1065 (PGU) confirmed real/correctly classified/no duplicate with 2 refs added (length 2,623 km + capacity 3,500 MMcf/d both high-tier); flagged 2 concerns — StartYear1=1993 matches no documented phase-completion date (spec), and Owner1='Petronas' 100% should likely be 'Petronas Gas Berhad', a separately listed, not-wholly-owned subsidiary (attribution); no blank fields safely fillable (Diameter is genuinely multi-valued across phases, left blank rather than forced).
